To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
metalation of porphin molecules at the solid-vaccuum interface is a surface-mediated in-situ reaction, which proceeds with high yield.

surface-mediated self-metalation of porphin molecules is a convenient way to tailor functional molecular architecture, and that this metalation can be monitored by scanning tunneling microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectrometry.

surface-mediated in situ metalation is a novel, convenient, and efficient way to tailor functional molecular structures, that the surface diffusion of the co-adsorbed metal is the key to the high yield of the corresponding reactions, and that the metalation of porphyin derivatives at the surface alters significantly the electronic properties and functionality of the porphyin molecule.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the exploration and characterization of the surface-mediated in situ metalation reaction of porphyrines.
the investigation of porphinoids at the solid-vaccuum interface.
the development and application of surface science techniques to study the adsorption, structure, and reactivity of porphyrinic molecules at the solid-vaccum interface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the in situ metalation is indeed a very efficient reaction and that the metalation of porphyrazines is generally faster than for porphyrins.

the metalation reaction proceeds via the transfer of a single hydrogen from the porphyrinic macrocycle to the central metal atom and that the activation barrier is mainly determined by the red-ox reaction.

the metalation of porphyins at the solid/vacuum interface is a surface-mediated process with a high yield and that it is possible to determine the corresponding activation barrier by surface science experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metalation of porphyin derivatives is generally a very fast reaction with a low activation barrier, and that the reaction is mediated by surface diffusion of the metal.
metalation reactions of free base porphyins can be conveniently realized at the solid-vaacuum interface by pre- and postmetalation with metal atoms.
the in situ metalation at the solid-vaccuum interface is a very efficient process with high yield and can significantly alter the adsorbate properties of the metalated porphyrins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metalation of porphyins at the solid surface is a surface-mediated reaction and that the metalation reaction is a surface-induced reaction.
metalation reactions at the solid-vaccuum interface can be very efficient, and the metalation can alter the electronic properties of the porphyin molecule significantly.
the metalation reaction of the free base porphin macrocycle is not limited to the gas phase but can be extended to the surface.
